newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: First Philippine Holdings delays debt issue.
newsitem.headline: First Philippine Holdings delays debt issue.

text.p: First Philippine Holdings Corporation told the Philippine Stock Exchange on Thursday it was postponing its proposed convertible note issue.

"Due to current adverse market conditions prevailing for Philippine issues, the Corporation and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell have decided to postpone the proposed convertible issue until conditions improve," the company said in a statement.
The statement did not state the size of the issue but earlier announcements had said it planned issue of $300 million worth of Euroconvertible notes.

First Philippine Holdings is the biggest shareholder in Manila Electric Co, the country's largest electricity distributor. The company also has interests in oil exploration, real estate and infrastructure.

The Philippines' financial markets have been rattled in the past few weeks in the wake of Thailand's financial crisis and on Wednesday the stocks as well as foreign exchange markets continued to be nervous.
Despite furious denials by government officials and the Central Bank, speculation that the peso may be devalued has persisted.
